# Doctern - AI Document OCR and Table Extraction

> Turns scanned documents into structured data, with table extraction that survives real-world scans.

Author: Muhammad Tanveer (Full-Stack AI Automation Engineer)
Contact: mtanveertahir66@gmail.com | https://www.linkedin.com/in/muhammad-tanveer-advenno/
Repository: https://github.com/haddindeve/doctern-document-ocr-ai
Source availability: implementation held in a private repository; access on request.

## Summary
Scanned documents hold data nobody can query. Generic OCR returns a wall of text and loses the table structure, which is usually the part that actually mattered.

An OCR pipeline that preserves layout, with a dedicated table-extraction stage so rows and columns survive as structure rather than being flattened into text. A web interface handles upload and review, because extraction from imperfect scans needs human confirmation.

## Stack
Backend: Python, OCR: Layout-aware recognition, Frontend: Web upload and review interface, Output: Structured exportable data

## Capabilities
- Layout-preserving OCR
- Table structure extraction
- Browser-based upload and review
- Structured export

## Outcomes
- Scanned tables recovered as data rather than flattened text
- Human review built into the flow instead of assumed-perfect extraction

## FAQ
Q: How is this different from ordinary OCR?
A: Ordinary OCR returns text and loses table structure. This pipeline recovers rows and columns as structure.

Q: What document types does it handle?
A: Scanned documents and PDFs where the useful content is tabular.

Q: Is extraction fully automatic?
A: Extraction is automatic; a review step lets a human confirm before export, which real-world scan quality requires.

Q: Is the source available?
A: Private repository.
